claims.claim: Under its registered criteria the full-recipe snack_box control did not pass: its maniptrans_sr was 0 and its ADD-AUC of 0.5639 was below the do-nothing baseline of 0.5662, although chord_sr was above 0.
The full-recipe snack_box control's ADD-AUC is within 0.01 of the do-nothing baseline, which the registration labels as a marginal result.
The registration says a marginal result does not take any of the SOP's causal branches, and the next step is then decided from diagnostic evidence or an additional seed.
The full-recipe snack_box policy succeeded under the task-native criteria in about 92% of 4096 worlds and its object position error was about 56 cm lower than that of leaving the object still.
The 1M-buffer snack_box policy had chord_sr 0 and ADD-AUC about 0.540, while the full-recipe snack_box policy had chord_sr about 0.922 and ADD-AUC about 0.564.
The 1M and full-recipe snack_box runs used the official recipe with byte-identical inputs and differ in configuration only in the replay buffer capacity and logging settings.
The improvement from the 1M snack_box run to the full-recipe snack_box run can be attributed to the larger replay buffer.
For the full-recipe snack_box policy, the shortfall against the do-nothing ADD-AUC comes from the static segments, as the Day 1b finding that the bar is dominated by static segments would predict.
About 317 of the first 440 static frames of the official snack_box sample are a prefix that was added upstream.
In this run, the official G1 recipe trained on the official snack_box sample did not exceed the do-nothing ADD-AUC.
The full-recipe snack_box policy was evaluated on 4096 worlds.
The full-recipe snack_box policy's ADD-AUC exceeded the do-nothing baseline.
